newsitem.title: USA: Texaco using second platform off Colombia.
newsitem.headline: Texaco using second platform off Colombia.

text.p: Texaco Inc said Monday it has begun using Chuchupa-B, the second offshore platform at the Chuchupa gas field offshore Colombia.

Chuchupa-B, located 10 miles from shore in 112 feet of water, started production on October 26 with the completion of the first of three horizontal wells. A second well has since been completed. Each of these wells is now producing at rates above 70 million cubic feet per day, Texaco said, adding a third well is currently nearing completion.
It said additional field development from the nine slot structure will be timed to meet demand.

Located 10 miles off Colombia's northeast coast, the Chuchupa field was discovered in 1973 and put in production in 1977. It is one of three natural gas fields operated by Texaco in Colombia's Guajira Province. Estimated remaining recoverable gas reserves from the three fields are in excess of four trillion cubic feet.

The Guajira natural gas fields are operated by Texaco under a 50/50 Association Contract with Ecopetrol, the Colombian national oil company, until December 31, 2004. After that date, Texaco will continue to operate the fields until 2016 under a recently negotiated BOMT (Build, Operate, Maintain and Transfer) agreement.
All of the natural gas produced is sold in the national market, Texaco said. -- New York Newsdesk 212-859-1610.
